newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: SBC Warburg sees 5.2 pct Argentine growth in '97.
newsitem.headline: SBC Warburg sees 5.2 pct Argentine growth in '97.

text.p: SBC Warburg on Tuesday forecast that Argentine gross domestic product would grow 5.2 percent next year, accelerating to 5.8 percent in 1998.
"The main engines of growth will be exports and investment in 1997, while consumption should begin to pick up in 1997 and early 1998," the investment bank said in a research note.
It predicted industrial production growth of an average 4.3 percent in 1997 and 7.0 percent the following year, while consumer inflation will remain very low at around 2.0 percent.

"Unfortunately the fiscal situation will continue to deteriorate. The operational fiscal deficit should grow to 1.8 percent of GDP," said SBC Warburg, comparing that to 1.13 percent of GDP forecast for this year.

It warned that tighter U.S. monetary policy in 1997 would mean the Peronist government, facing mid-term elections, could find it "very challenging to externally finance the fiscal deficit, while rolling over debt amortizations."
